summary.intent: Clear a large backlog of ~105 open issues on the cipherbox repo by mapping file-collision surfaces, batching issues into parallelizable PRs, decomposing an underspecified umbrella issue (#635) into schedulable sub-issues, launching multiple worktree agents to implement PRs, and running an unattended CodeRabbit review queue (rate-limited to 1/hr) while the user was AFK.
summary.outcome: Minted 10 new tracking/delivery issues (#1014-#1020, #1025, #1026, #1028, #1029) with verified dependency edges under #635; shipped and merged 5 PRs (#1021, #1022, #1023, #1024, #1027) covering 24 issues including #719; caught and fixed 3 latent HIGH-severity bugs (reseal.rs epoch mismatch, two rule-8 encode/decode redaction violations, a resource-cap bypass, a dropped timeout) before they shipped; resolved a semantic (non-textual) merge conflict between #1023 and #1027 that git's merge-tree didn't surface; left 4 decisions and a wave-2 queue (8 PRs, ~25 issues) for the user.

repo: `crates/engine/src/facade.rs` and `crates/engine/tests/write_plane.rs` are hotspots touched by nearly every engine cluster — the real cap on parallelism, not issue count

`crates/engine/src/rotation/` (~6300 lines) and `crates/engine/src/grants/` (~2600 lines) already implement nearly all named primitives; production wiring falls through `EngineError::Unimplemented` at facade.rs:1901 — do not re-implement primitives, only wire them

AGENTS.md rule 8 requires encode/decode symmetry for optional typed keys combined with merge_unknown's presence-based precedence guard — this is a recurring trap (hit twice independently in one night: writeScopeSeed and expiresAt)
Secret-bearing payload types should derive over `SecretBytes` (redacted Debug + constant-time PartialEq) rather than hand-rolling a `SecretField` newtype — established by #1003/#1021
Redaction tests must pin whole-string goldens, not marker/byte-spelling counts — a raw `[u8;32]` field defaulting to zero bytes can slip past a hex-substring search
Entropy and time must enter engine code only through seams (`crate::entropy::Entropy::fill`, injected `UnixMillis`) — a direct OsRng/SystemTime call breaks the KAT regime

CodeRabbit edits ONE status comment in place rather than posting a new one — must re-fetch before concluding a review is walkthrough-only vs a real pass; timing checks near the exact hour boundary can read stale state

git merge-tree reporting zero conflicts does not guarantee compile success — trait signature changes (e.g. adding `max_bytes` to `RecordTransport::get_record`) can merge textually clean while breaking downstream impls (matches prior repo incidents #779/#782, #944/#946)

`gate::floor::check` rejects records below the durable epoch floor, which directly contradicts the sweep's purpose of converging exactly those below-floor records — unresolved design tension logged as #1025
CHILL CodeRabbit review profile has been acceptable to the user so far; Greptile is inaccessible until mid-August quota reset

code.finding: fanout_get_verify signature changed from returning (u64, bytes) to (VerifiedRecord, bytes) in #997/#1021, rippling into liveness.rs, publish.rs, resolve.rs, pointer_fetch.rs, settings.rs, sync/drain.rs

Write body structure signature was signed at the write epoch while the gate recomputes preimages at the read epoch; a read rotation separates the two, meaning first production revocation would sign a permanently unadoptable scope root — fixed in #1027 by making the signing closure epoch-agnostic
RootAdopter hard-coded parent_node_seed: None, which the gate treats as a fail-closed ascent-link mismatch, making real descendant resolution impossible — fixed in #1027

GrantBlobPayload, OverrideSeedPayload (line 300), OwnerWriteBlobPayload (line 433), HistoryLinkPayload (line 669) converted to derive over SecretBytes instead of hand-rolled redacted Debug + non-constant-time PartialEq

refresh() single-flight leader logic at :211-248; later reshaped by #1021 into json_authed/request_authed helpers, then #1023 threaded timeout_ms/credentials through the same helpers causing a semantic (not just textual) rebase conflict

maxBytes cap comparisons were bypassable via NaN/Infinity since both `declared > maxBytes` and `total + value.byteLength > maxBytes` evaluate false for non-finite values — fixed with Number.isSafeInteger guard at top of drainCapped
contract crate's Http seam impl was silently dropping timeout_ms, letting calls the engine bounded to CONTROL_TIMEOUT_MS run to the full 30s client budget instead

Only ChildIndexResolver (:361) and ScopeRootPublisher (:385) of six rotation seam traits have production impls; SweepResolver, WriteWavePublisher, CascadeResealResolver, WriteSubtreeResolver remain faked

workflow: When fanning out recon agents before a large batching decision, run them in parallel and synthesize a corrected keystone ranking afterward — the initial manual read of issue text (#846, #635 sizing) was wrong until agents verified against the actual tree
Before flipping a draft PR to ready-for-review under a rate-limited external reviewer, re-draft immediately after a review lands with findings so the fix-push doesn't consume the next slot

Delegate PR-review-finding triage to a sub-agent instructed to verify findings rather than blindly apply suggested diffs — this caught a factually wrong CodeRabbit premise (SeededEntropy determinism) and a structurally unworkable suggested fix (expiry enforcement)
When splitting a PR post-hoc (crypto vs mechanical), resume the same agent that authored the original commits rather than doing fresh git surgery, since it knows which commits carry which change
After any force-push/rebase in a worktree, verify with two-dot vs three-dot diff comparison that the file count actually dropped, confirming the merge-base moved

Test a proposed merge order with `git merge-tree` AND an actual `cargo check`/full build in a scratch worktree before trusting textual cleanliness alone, since trait-shape changes can merge clean but not compile
Clean up scratch worktrees and merged-branch worktrees promptly once their purpose is served, and check for stale worktrees left from older abandoned branches

friction: Initial state check misread #1022's CodeRabbit status comment mid-flight (checked 00:27Z, comment updated 00:28:25Z) — user had to correct with a screenshot; CodeRabbit's in-place comment editing makes read timing brittle near the rate-limit boundary
A crypto-fix commit (76dc4465f) missed the #1022 merge window by exactly one second, stranding it on the split-off #1021 branch and requiring detection + a rebase to recover it

#1023's rebase hit a conflict git's merge-tree did not report: #1027 added a test decorator implementing RecordTransport against the pre-fork 3-parameter get_record, while #1023 added a required max_bytes parameter to that same trait method — textually clean, semantically broken (E0050/E0061)

The agent's first pre-flight check for #1023's rebase safety only searched for new HttpRequest literal construction sites and missed the RecordTransport trait-shape change entirely, giving false confidence
Second commit in the #1021 worktree used --no-verify because the worktree had no node_modules, so lint-staged couldn't run — flagged as a caveat but not resolved
Agent's first cargo test run in the #1023 rebase was piped through tail, masking the real exit code and truncating the log to 9 of 36 suites — had to be re-run to get accurate pass counts
Assistant's own file-overlap check for merge ordering initially raced (branches not fully fetched) and merge-tree errored silently, producing meaningless zero-conflict counts that had to be redone
